issues.description: Return-type inconsistency for PersonService.getAllPersons: the template declares getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions) to return List<Person>, and the client (both template and solution) and PersonResource expect the endpoint to return a List<Person> (JSON array). However, the solution's PersonService.getAllPersons implementation returns a java.util.stream.Stream<Person>. This mismatch (Stream vs List) is structural and prevents PersonResource from returning the expected List<Person> or will require additional collection/serialization steps; it will confuse students and may lead to compilation errors or incorrect server responses.
issues.suggested_fix:
Align the PersonService.getAllPersons signature and return type with the rest of the code and the problem description. Two reasonable fixes:
1) Change PersonService.getAllPersons to return List<Person> (as in the template). Implement sorting on a copy of the internal list and return a List (e.g., Collections.unmodifiableList(sortedList) or new ArrayList<>(sortedList)). Update implementation accordingly. This keeps the server endpoint returning a JSON array matching the client expectations.
2) Alternatively, if a Stream return is desired, update PersonResource to collect the Stream into a List before returning (e.g., personService.getAllPersons(...).collect(Collectors.toList())) and ensure the service interface in template/documentation is updated to indicate Stream<Person>. Option (1) is preferred because the template and client already expect List<Person>.
